rows.en: Melvi: "Oh, Big Brother Touya! Good morning!"
Touya: "Y-yeah, good morning... You're full of energy again today, Melvi."
Ymir: "Good morning, Touya."
Touya: "Ymir... Are you all right?"
Ymir: "Yes. I'm sorry I worried you.
I'm all right now. Thanks to Melvi."
Melvi: "Hee hee hee hee."
Yamato: "You look like a mother today, Ymir.
With Melvi sitting on your lap and everything."
Forzen: "Hm? Does that make you my wife, then?
Just kidding. Ha ha ha ha... O-ow, ow, ow!"
Paldia: "What are you talking about?
...Still, I'm glad you're feeling better, Ymir.
Now, shall we have breakfast?"
Ymir: "Oh, I'll help too."
Melvi: "Melvi too!"
Paldia: "Then let's all get things ready."
Melvi: "Okaaay! Come on, Yamato!"
Touya: "...Hey, about what we discussed yesterday...
Have you told everyone?"
Forzen: "No. That is for Ymir to decide.
Melvi will go on living with her as family,
so she has a right to know. As for you..."
Touya: "Me...?"
Forzen: "In the not-too-distant future,
you'll be my brother-in-law, after all."
Touya: "B-brother-in-law...?"
Forzen: "Oh? Am I mistaken?
Ymir doesn't seem entirely opposed to the idea..."
Paldia: "Oh? What are you two talking about?
You're not plotting something improper again, are you?"
Forzen: "Certainly not. We were just discussing
our plans for a bright future."
Paldia: "Honestly, what are you saying?
Touya, I don't know what he's told you,
but don't let it bother you. He's always like this."
Forzen: "How cruel."
Touya: "Yes. I know that."
Forzen: "Hey, you too...?"
Ymir: "Heh heh heh..."
Ymir: "Well, we'll be off."
Melvi: "See you laaater!"
Yamato: "Huh? You're nyot asking to come along today."
Melvi: "Hee hee! It's a se-cret. Right, Mama?"
Paldia: "Riiight."
Ymir: "Heh heh... Then I'll look forward to it."
Melvi: "Yeah!"
Ymir: "..."
Touya: "..."
Ymir: "...Touya?"
Touya: "Hm?"
Ymir: "What do you think I should do from now on?"
Touya: "Huh? What's brought this on?"
Ymir: "...Melvi told me that no matter whose child I am,
I'm still her big sister...
Hearing that made me so happy.
But the blood of the person who caused that tragedy
flows through my body... How can someone like me
work for world peace...?"
Touya: "...Are you serious?
Melvi's right. You're still Ymir, aren't you?
Besides, you weren't the one who caused the incident."
Ymir: "That's true, but..."
Touya: "Isn't what matters most not what you've done in the past,
but what you're going to do from now on?"
Ymir: "Touya..."
Touya: "Besides, if you quit here and now,
you'd be running away.
That wouldn't solve anything.
You've gotta see this through with Ze=Ode.
...Though I guess I'm not one to talk so high and mighty."
Ymir: "No... That's not true.
You're right. Perhaps I was trying to run away...
Yes. I have to do this.
To prove that Dr. Wenimas... That my mother fought
for peace, and that she truly wished
for peace throughout the world."
Touya: "Yeah. First, you've gotta believe
in Dr. Wenimas yourself. If you do, then no matter what anyone says,
you'll be able to hold on to who you are. Won't you?"
Ymir: "Yeah... Thank you.
I'm glad I talked to you...
If anything else happens, will you listen to me again?"
Touya: "Of course. If you're all right with me."
Ymir: "...I'm glad."
Touya: "Now, about telling everyone..."
Ymir: "Yes. I'll tell them properly.
So... Could you give me... just a little courage?"
Touya: "...?"
Ymir: "..."
Touya: (Th-this situation...)
Ymir: "Touya..."
Touya: "Huh? No... W-well...
You can't just spring that on me... I've gotta prepare myself..."
Ymir: "..."
Touya: (Y-Ymir's face is so close...)
Ymir: "...Like this..."
Touya: "...Huh?"
Ymir: "Hold my hand like this... Please?"
Touya: "Ha, ha ha ha... Y-your hand.
Y-yeah. If that's all, then anytime..."
Ymir: "?"
Yamato: "Hey, are you really all right?"
Ymir: "Huh? Y-yes..."
Yamato: "It's nyot good to keep it all to yourself."
Ymir: "...Thank you. I'm very fortunate.
Even though I'm the daughter of a Ze=Ode researcher,
there are people who worry about me and encourage me..."
Touya: "..."
Ymir: "Yesterday... Melvi encouraged me.
She said that no matter whose child I am, I'm still her big sister.
Hearing that made me so happy..."
Yamato: "I see... Melvi's a good girl, isn't she?"
Ymir: "Yes. She's very kind.
At that moment, with so many people who care about me,
I wondered what I was doing.
So I decided to face what Dr. Wenimas... What my mother
had been trying to do."
Yamato: "You're strong."
Ymir: "That's right. I'm strong.
I have to... be strong..."
Touya: "Hey, don't push yourself too hard.
There are other people who worry about you too.
Right here, for one."
Ymir: "Touya... Thank you."
Yamato: "Hey, are you going to tell everyone about this?"
Ymir: "Yes. I'll tell them properly."
Yamato: "I see. Yeah. That's for the best.
Good luck, Ymir!"
Ymir: "Heh heh. Thank you."
Ymir: "I'm not sure how to answer that..."
Ai: "So what if you're the daughter of a researcher from a hundred years ago?
So what if you're that Wenimas person's daughter?"
Ymir: "..."
Ai: "Being someone's daughter doesn't invalidate
who you are. You're Ymir.
Nothing more and nothing less, right?"
Ymir: "Heh heh heh heh..."
Ai: "Wh-what? Did I say something weird?
I thought I said something pretty good..."
Ymir: "Oh, I'm sorry.
Melvi said something similar to me yesterday...
And I just found it funny..."
Clovis: "So Ai thinks on the same level
as a twelve-year-old girl."
Ai: "Hey! I was trying to cheer her up!"
Ymir: "Heh heh... I'm sorry.
...Ai, thank you."
Ivel: "...Everyone, I am sorry.
Because I kept silent..."
Xiujian: "We understand how you feel.
Please do not blame yourself."
Arthur: "Indeed. We will remain her companions,
for as long as she wishes."
Ivel: "Thank you."
Fain: "...By the way, what happened to her?"
Ivel: "Her?"
Fain: "You know, that cheeky, stuck-up woman."
Ivel: "Oh. She's in the capital at the moment..."
Ivel: "...Excuse me.
...Yes. Yes, they are all here.
What? ...Understood. Please put it through here."
Fain: "Is something the matter?"
Ivel: "There is a transmission for you.
I will connect it to that monitor now."
Maki: "Hey there!"
Fain: "Maki..."
Maki: "Hey, why do you look so disappointed?
Who did you think it was?"
Fain: "N-no one! Anyway, what's the matter?"
Maki: "Something a little urgent came up.
I asked them to make an exception and put me through."
Touya: "What happened?"
Maki: "The Agarthian and Zigrim armies are fighting
near the border right now. I got information that Type-G weapons
have been transported to a Zigrim garrison."
Touya: "Type-G? What's that?"
Celica: "...It's a general term for weapons that act on the nervous system
and can destroy the mechanisms that transmit nerve signals."
Clovis: "Chemical weapons... I didn't know
they had those over here too..."
Celica: "They were disposed of long ago.
Even before I was born, the League Treaty
had already banned their use.
So current Armored Mechs aren't fitted
with countermeasures. Their purification systems can offer some protection,
but they shouldn't be able to neutralize them completely.
Even aboard a Spirit Mech, you probably wouldn't come out unscathed."
Arthur: "So their effectiveness comes from being weapons of the past..."
Maki: "Of course I warned the Agarthian Army too,
but there seems to be a move to let Zigrim use them,
then use that as grounds to isolate Zigrim."
Celica: "Surely my brother wouldn't...?"
Maki: "I don't think so. Personally, I suspect
someone like Colonel Geel. Anyway,
if those things are used, the frontline soldiers won't survive.
I can't let that happen.
I know it's selfish of me to ask,
but you're the only people I can turn to."
Ivel: "...This has gone beyond
a dispute between nations.
We cannot allow such things to be used.
...I am sorry, but it seems
we must ask you to go."
Ymir: "...Lady Ivel, are you truly certain?"
Ivel: "This is a matter that concerns the entire world.
It will mean resolving it by force,
but I see no other choice. I am counting on you."
Maki: "Thank you.
...I'll send the garrison's coordinates
to the Liebhofen. I'll be in touch again."
Ai: "She seemed to be in a hurry."
Celica: "The ones fighting on the front line now are Lieutenant Colonel Selg and..."
Fain: "Oh! Master!"
Aurelie: "I see. I doubt that's her only reason,
but it seems to be a pretty big part of it."
Touya: "Anyway, let's do something about those weapons."
Ymir: "Yes. Let's hurry."
Melvi: "Huh? Everyone's in such a hurry...
Hmm... Are they going to launch?
But I went to all that trouble to make packed lunches..."
Mechanic A: "Hurry up and load the supplies! We don't know
when we'll be back next."
Melvi: "...Huh?"
Mechanic F: "We're going to a Zigrim garrison this time, right?
Will we be all right with the forces we have?"
Mechanic B: "A rapid assault is probably our only option.
However good the Spirit Mechs are, against an army,
we'll be at a disadvantage in a prolonged battle."
Mechanic F: "It's a shame we're short on pilots."
Mechanic C: "Ahti's one thing,
but Forstin's as good as new..."
Mechanic A: "Come on, come on! You've stopped working!
We're sailing soon. Hurry!"
Melvi: "...Melvi can do it too... All right!"
Steinies: "Calling me all the way out here...
Is the front line all right, Lieutenant Colonel?"
Fores: "Shut up, Steinies!
You left the front without permission, and now you're going
to use those things?! What are you thinking?!"
Steinies: "Who knows? I'm afraid I have no idea
what you're talking about."
Fores: "You..."
Reamond: "Don't, Colonel. He..."
Steinies: "Heh heh. That lieutenant of yours
seems to understand the situation better.
You don't have the authority to give me orders now.
Besides, this is war. There's no point if you don't win."
Fores: "Yes, war means killing one another. I have no intention
of pretending to be some saint now. But using Type-G weapons
is an act of folly that violates basic humanity!
Think again! Come to your senses, Steinies!!"
Steinies: "It's because you keep dragging things out,
playing at war forever and ever,
that Agarthia thinks it can look down on us.
You're the one who needs to wake up, Colonel."
Reamond: "Captain, the enemy will not be the only ones
to suffer. Our own allies on the front line will be affected too.
Furthermore, ordinary civilians who are not soldiers will die.
That would leave a stain
on your own record, you know."
Steinies: "I'm just carrying out the President's orders.
Besides, a record is something the incompetent bring up
so they can cling to past glories.
What's the point of waving that around?
In this world, power is everything. Heh heh heh."
Fores: "..."
Steinies: "...Take this gun, for example.
Even that Growster would be nothing
but a lump of meat if I pulled this trigger.
Rank, fame, money... None of it matters.
The strong survive. That's all."
Reamond: "...You are..."
Steinies: "Heh heh heh... I can just picture those Agarthian bastards
coughing up blood and writhing in agony... Even the soldiers
will be sacrifices for victory. It's what they'd want, right?"
Fores: "Y-you bastard...!!"
Steinies: "Whoa, that's far enough.
I told you already. Just because you outrank me,
that doesn't give you the authority to interfere with what I do.
If you want to stop me, get the President's approval.
If you can't, you can stand there and watch how I fight!
Heh heh... Haaahahahaha!!"
Reamond: "...What a frightening man
this Steinies is."
Fores: "He's a disgrace to Zigrim... Damn it!"
Reamond: "...Quite right."
Melvi: "Huh? Where... am I?
...Oh, well!"
Fores: "...That sound just now..."
Reamond: "No readings.
It must be the Liebhofen, as we suspected.
It seems information leaked out."
Fores: "...But perhaps it is for the best this time.
If they can stop him here..."
Reamond: "Then we will simply watch from the sidelines... No,
I suppose we cannot."
Fores: "Exactly. Besides, if it comes to it,
we will have to stop him ourselves."
Reamond: "Then shall we head for the garrison...?"
Fores: "Yes. But be careful, Lieutenant.
There's no telling what Steinies might do."
Reamond: "Yes. I know that. All too well..."
Baren: "...We'll arrive shortly."
Celica: "That's it... It's quite large, isn't it?"
Ymir: "To think they'd built a base like this..."
Melvi: "...Hmm... Huh? Where is this...?
Oh! A Spirit Mech!"
Melvi: "Is that... the mech they were talking about?
...I wonder if it'll move?"

review_batches.context: Complete 314-row member examined, covering Ymir's family disclosure and alternate encouragement routes, Maki's warning, Melvi's decision and the Zigrim confrontation. This slice covers breakfast and the first Ymir/Touya discussion.
review_batches.decisions: Restore Melvi as the child on Ymir's lap, not the reverse. Keep Big Brother/Big Sister as affectionate addresses rather than new sibling facts, Forzen's brother-in-law tease as a joke, Ymir's distress and Touya's distinction between parentage and personal deeds. Mother Wenimas is now explicit. Do not invent a confirmed engagement or details of yesterday's unseen disclosure.

row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0013d.l00: Yamato likens Ymir to a mother because Melvi is on Ymir's lap. Restore the omitted sitting subject correctly; no biological motherhood asserted.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0016e.l00: Forzen immediately says he is joking. Preserve the wife tease and pain reaction without inventing a specific blow or a real remarriage.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o002b5.l00: Yesterday's discussion is referenced but not recapitulated here. Touya asks whether the others have been told.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o002fd.l01: Melvi has a right to know because they remain family. Do not invent an adoption or reverse which child belongs to Forzen and Paldia.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0036c.l01: Brother-in-law is Forzen's teasing prediction, not proof of engagement or a completed marriage. Paldia tells Touya not to take his talk seriously.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0050b.l00: You too is a deliberately clipped complaint at Touya joining Paldia's teasing, not an accidentally omitted English action.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o005f2.l00: The secret is shared with Mama/Paldia and later pays off as packed lunches. Do not invent a hidden mission here.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00763.l00: Her big sister is Melvi's affectionate address to her aunt Ymir, not a change in their biological relationship.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00763.l03: Ymir fears inherited association with the person who caused the tragedy. Do not supply a new named culprit, deliberate intent or shared personal guilt.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0080d.l02: Touya explicitly distinguishes Ymir herself from the person who caused the incident. Keep that distinction.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0087b.l00: Past acts versus future choices is Touya's stated argument; do not turn it into narration excusing every past action by every character.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00962.l03: Dr. Wenimas is explicitly called Mother. Preserve the correction and the wish to prove her peaceful intent as Ymir's purpose, not proof already furnished.

review_batches.context: Two alternate Ymir encouragement paths, her disclosure to the group, Ivel's apology and Fain's question about an unnamed woman. Read all 314 rows, including the handholding payoff and Maki's actual arrival.
review_batches.decisions: Preserve the request for courage as a request to hold hands, without adding a kiss or act. Keep the alternate Yamato route separate, the source's open/close quotation across 113-117, Ai's rounded hundred-year reference, Clovis's exact twelve-year-old joke and the conditional continued friendship. No unnamed woman's identity is supplied.

row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00a76.l02: Ymir asks Touya to hear future concerns. He agrees; do not reverse who seeks support.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00c91.l00: Hold my hand is the explicit payoff. Do not add a kiss, erotic action or agreement not present in the source.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00d3c.l00: Separate Yamato-involved encouragement route starts here; not forced to occur after the prior handholding route.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00ea4.l00: Source quote opens here and continues through a separately addressed following command/page group at 114-117. Preserve the unmatched opening here and unmatched closing at 117 rather than adding new quotation marks.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o00f79.l02: Right here is a deliberate short emphasis referring to Touya himself as another person who worries about Ymir.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01100.l00: Ai says a hundred years as a rounded conversational reference. Do not silently change her spoken number to 109.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01272.l00: Clovis jokes that Ai thinks like a twelve-year-old, referring to Melvi. Exact age retained; no global narrator judgment of intelligence.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01382.l01: Companionship continues as long as Ymir wishes; this is not a condition that she must obey Ivel.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0140e.l00: Cheeky, stuck-up woman remains unnamed in this exchange. Do not insert a future identity from profile knowledge.

review_batches.context: Maki transmission and Type-G warning, Ivel's authorization, Melvi's lunches/resolve, mechanics' pilot shortage and start of Steinies confrontation. Full member read before drafting.
review_batches.decisions: Keep G classification fictional, nervous-system action broad, treaty ban before Celica's birth, partial purification-system protection versus full neutralization and Spirit Mech risk. Maki suspects Colonel Geel; do not certify a conspiracy or blame Lodis. Preserve all requests, garrison-coordinate destination, Rest implication without a new identity in the dialogue, separate Ahti/Forstin state and ranks.

row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01460.l02: Ivel requests the incoming transmission be routed to the current location; no outgoing message is being sent by the translation tool.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01529.l00: Maki's familiar older-sister-style address is rendered by her established given name, consistent with s_008. No biological sister relationship invented.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o015de.l01: Reported shipment of Type-G weapons to a Zigrim garrison is Maki's intelligence. Do not add a specific chemical agent, quantity, delivery method or deployment time.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0165a.l00: Translate the broad fictional effect on nervous signal transmission only; no real-world chemical specification or operational instructions added.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o016d3.l01: League Treaty is the shortened source reference to the existing International League Treaty term. Ban predates Celica's birth; no year invented.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o016d3.l04: Purification offers partial protection but cannot fully neutralize the weapons, according to Celica. Keep uncertainty and the warning that Spirit Mechs are not complete protection.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o017b7.l00: Maki already warned the Agarthian Army. Her report of a faction wanting Zigrim politically isolated is not proof every commander shares the plan.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01825.l00: Maki thinks Lodis is not responsible and suspects someone like Geel. Both are qualified opinions, not proven assignments of blame.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01825.l04: Maki asks the party for help; do not turn it into her volunteering to attack the garrison.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01961.l02: Ivel reluctantly accepts a forceful intervention and asks them to act. Do not invent a declaration of general war on Zigrim.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o019b1.l02: Coordinates go to the Liebhofen. No actual coordinate values appear here and none are invented.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01a4e.l00: Master is Fain's recognition in context, consistent with Rest's profile. Keep the source address rather than adding his name to an unnamed line.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01a69.l00: Aurelie thinks concern for that person is a major factor in Maki's urgency, but not her only reason. No single-motive certainty.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01b36.l02: Packed lunches are Melvi's effort and earlier secret; no specific food item or promise invented.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01c8c.l00: Ahti is contrasted with nearly new Forstin. Do not assign an unmentioned exact damage level to Ahti.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01d48.l01: Fores is a lieutenant colonel, Steinies a captain, Reamond a first lieutenant. Colonel/Lieutenant in later direct address are natural shortened English forms, not promotions.

review_batches.context: Final 74 rows: Fores/Reamond object to Steinies, his claimed presidential authority and threats, Melvi's wrong turn and arrival at the base. Read the entire source member.
review_batches.decisions: Retain killing, civilian/allied casualties, the gun/lump-of-meat threat, blood/agony language and abusive contempt without softening or inventing actual deaths. Keep claims of presidential orders as claims, rank separate from current command authority, Fores's possible intervention and Reamond's Quite right catchphrase. Three timing rows use the narrowly validated punctuation-only mapping with every original wait retained.

row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01e49.l02: Rank and present command authority are distinct. Steinies claims she cannot order him now; do not conclude he outranks her.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01ec0.l00: Fores acknowledges war involves killing and rejects hypocrisy, while condemning Type-G use as inhuman. Preserve all parts.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o01fa0.l02: Reamond explicitly warns of civilian deaths as well as harm to both armies. Do not soften civilians into mere collateral inconvenience.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0202f.l00: Presidential orders are Steinies's claim. Do not mark them independently verified or invent a signed directive.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o020d7.l01: Threat imagines even Growster reduced to a lump of meat by the gun. Preserve the brutality as hypothetical speech; no actual shooting occurs in the text.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o02172.l00: Steinies imagines Agarthians coughing blood and writhing in agony. Retain the full force of his cruelty without adding new gore or narrating that it has happened.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o02172.l02: He calls soldiers sacrifices for victory and claims it would be their wish; this is his contemptuous rationale, not assent from those soldiers.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o022ff.l00: Quite right preserves Reamond's established agreement/catchphrase without doubling a single occurrence.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o02357.l00: Melvi's wrong turn is consistent with her profile's poor sense of direction. Do not invent a deliberate planned infiltration route.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o023bf.l01: Reamond infers Liebhofen from no readings and a sound, not a confirmed visual identification.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o02403.l01: Fores hopes the party can stop Steinies; this does not mean she formally joins them here.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0246f.l00: If necessary, Fores/Reamond must stop him themselves. Preserve willingness to intervene, rather than portraying unconditional support for his plan.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0260b.l00: Punctuation-only timing row; each two-dot leader becomes two ASCII periods with every FC:02:3E control and physical row preserved.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0260b.l01: Second original timing row retained independently, not merged or shortened.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0260b.l02: Third original timing row retained independently. These effects count as nonempty rows but are not prose translations.
row_decisions.scenario.s_013.o0276b.l00: Melvi recognizes the previously discussed mech but does not identify its name in this line. Her question about whether it works remains tentative.
